A planned rebuild of the legacy FAST scheduling workflow for athlete sleep and team travel. The repository name is institution-neutral; the initial use case remains Baylor athletes and team travel.

## Current status

Research and static installer inspection are complete. Product discovery is underway, with four unanswered questions recorded in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). No application or forecasting engine has been implemented or validated.

Start with:

- [Agent context and checkpoint](AGENTS.md)
- [Research report](FAST-MODERNIZATION-RESEARCH.md)
- [Proposed specification](SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md)
- [Installer inspection findings](installer-inspection/FINDINGS.md)

The specification contains proposals, not approved product decisions. Repository creation does not authorize implementation or resolve the paused interview.

## Archive boundary

This private repository tracks authored project documentation, inspection scripts, and future application code, tests, and synthetic fixtures. Original installers, proprietary binaries, bundled manuals/schema, screenshots, and staff/team schedules remain outside Git.

On the original Windows workstation the archive is located at:

```text
G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\99_UNSORTED\From_Desktop\TECHNOLOGY\FAST
```

Historical documents contain relative links into that archive. Links to `payload/`, `help/`, inventories, or original materials require local archive access; those assets are intentionally absent from a clone. Missing archive links do not mean extraction failed.

The active development checkout is outside OneDrive:

```text
C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\sleep-scheduler
```

## Inspection script

`installer-inspection/map-payload.ps1` maps already-extracted cabinet members to their original filenames and verifies sizes/hashes against the MSI. It does not install FAST or extract the cabinet. Supply `-ArchiveRoot` pointing to the archive above; its `installer-inspection/cab-raw/` must already exist. Generated payload and inventories are ignored by Git. The script refuses to overwrite an existing output payload.

## Development direction

Resolve the pending product interview, prototype one complete scheduling comparison, then finalize the specification and implementation tasks. Keep sleep opportunity distinct from actual sleep and preserve explicit model provenance for any future forecasts.

content.text:
Branch is clean and synced with origin.

**Sanity check run:** full suite 67/67 passing, CLI executes end-to-end on both the fixture dates and shifted dates, working tree clean, branch pushed.

## What I did

The FAST schedule builder is `sleep-scheduler/` — it had three long research documents and **zero code**. The paused design interview was blocking everything, so I built the slice that's identical under every possible answer to those questions, and left the questions for you.

**Six modules, written test-first against the spec's own acceptance table (67 tests):**

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| `temporal.py` | local wall time + IANA zone → UTC instant; half-open intervals; merge/subtract |
| `schedule.py` | Event, ProtectedSleepWindow, AssumptionSet, Scenario |
| `opportunity.py` | spec steps 1–8, conflicts, scenario comparison |
| `adapter.py` | forecast seam — the only adapter returns a *status*, never a number |
| `persistence.py` | JSON round-trip preserving the zone each time was entered in |
| `cli.py` | `python -m sleep_scheduler <baseline> <candidate>` |

The runnable example is the spec's own first workflow — a late-return comparison showing **5h25m** of overnight opportunity with the lift at 07:00 vs **7h55m** at 09:30, a **+2h30m** difference against an 8h target, with the forecast explicitly marked unavailable. Fixtures are synthetic; I didn't touch the `G:` archive.

**Two defects caught in review, both of which silently produced a *better* number:**
- `Event.mandatory` used a whitelist, so an event kind not on it (`"film"`, or a typo like `"trainng"`) vanished from the calculation entirely — no conflict, no blocked sleep. Inverted so mandatory is the default.
- The CLI's default reporting window was hardcoded to the fixture dates; any other scenario reported 0h opportunity and a full shortfall with no error. Now derived from the scenario span.

Also worth knowing: `zoneinfo` does **not** refuse impossible local times — `2026-03-08 02:30` Chicago silently becomes 03:30. `LocalTime` raises on that and on ambiguous autumn times. That's recorded in STATUS gotchas.

## The four questions I didn't answer for you

Q1 (late-return is the first workflow) and Q2 (opportunity-only for v1) I assumed from the spec — each is a one-line reversal. Q4 (who operates/approves) doesn't bite yet since nothing exports.

**Q3 — who is modelled: a representative athlete, subgroups, or individuals?** — is the one actually blocking. Everything person-shaped is deferred behind it: `AthleteProfile`, group membership, subgroup obligations, scenario revisions. That's also two of the four uncovered acceptance rows.

## Where it lives

Branch `worktree-calendar-core`, pushed to `erash11/sleep-scheduler`. **Not merged to main** — main's `docs/STATUS.md` is still the empty one until you merge. PR: https://github.com/erash11/sleep-scheduler/pull/new/worktree-calendar-core

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m sleep_scheduler \
  fixtures/late-return-baseline.json fixtures/late-return-candidate.json
```
